title: Robust Two-Qubit Geometric Phase Gates Using Amplitude and Frequency Ramping in Trapped Ions
author: C. M. Bowers et al. / LLNL & NIST Ion Storage Group
key_claims: Ramped detuning and amplitude modulation of state-dependent forces enable robust trapped-ion two-qubit geometric phase gates
Gate protocol captures robustness of far-detuned operation while retaining speed from near-resonant phases
Ions operate at higher temperatures with reduced calibration overhead, paving way for scalable ion-trap quantum computers
Phase-space trajectory control ensures motional state returns to origin, leaving only entangling phase shift
methodology: Radio-frequency and microwave electromagnetic fields applied to trapped ions; ramped detuning through resonance; amplitude ramping; phase-space tomography
key_risk: Demonstrated in a specific ion-trap apparatus; transferability to multi-zone scalable architectures (e.g., Quantinuum, IonQ) requires further validation
next_experiment: Implement in shielded multi-zone trap with extra hardware; benchmark gate fidelity at scale; integrate with QPilotos router for distributed ion-trap quantum networking
notes: Directly relevant to C9 Quantum Bridge and QPilotos backends. The ramped-detuning principle (start far, approach resonance, retreat) is analogous to simulated annealing and could inspire optimization heuristics in C9's hypothesis debate module.
